missing_spec_content.spec_text: Reaction times vary from person to person.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson gives a typical range ('For an alert driver, it is usually 0.2–0.9 seconds', keyPoints[1].content) and factors that lengthen reaction time. It never states that reaction times vary from one person to another.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: interpret and evaluate measurements from simple methods to measure the different reaction times of students
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson only shows repeat results for one student ('Example results: ruler-drop reaction times for one student', tables[1].title). It does not show how to compare or evaluate reaction times between different students. It also does not explain how a ruler-drop distance becomes a time.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: (Physics only) Students will be required to interpret graphs relating speed to stopping distance for a range of vehicles.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson only says such graphs exist ('Graphs of stopping distance against speed can be drawn for different vehicles. On such a graph you can read each vehicle's stopping distance at a given speed and compare them.', keyPoints[0].content). No graph is given and no interpretation is practised.

factual_errors.text: In emergency braking, the deceleration is very high. Then the forces on passengers are very large. This is why seatbelts and crumple zones are essential.
factual_errors.correction: Crumple zones only reduce forces in a collision, by deforming and increasing the time of impact. They play no part during braking. Seatbelts do restrain passengers during heavy braking. Crumple zones should not be given as a reason linked to braking deceleration.

not_checked: keyPoints[0].tutor_note refers to 'a diagram of a car journey from hazard to stop', but every keyPoint has "diagram": null. No such diagram exists to check.
introTips[4] makes a real-world claim that could not be checked against the specification or verified: 'That is why motorway speed limits save so many lives.'
